Gastric Adenocarcinoma The patient was admitted to the People's Hospital of Zhejiang Province complaining of abdominal pain that had persisted for 2 months and had worsened in the past week. The patient was diagnosed with gastric adenocarcinoma and was evaluated as inoperable. Palliative chemotherapy treatment was initiated along with apatinib, which was well-tolerated with only Grade 2 neutropenia and Grade 1 vomiting observed during treatment. The CT scan performed post-treatment indicated partial response to chemotherapy. The patient underwent total gastrectomy, D2 lymph node dissection, and Roux-en-Y anastomosis after being evaluated for acceptable radical surgery. The postoperative pathology report indicates no residual cancer tissue found in the resected tissue sample. The patient recovered well post-surgery and underwent maintenance treatment with apatinib in the same dose as before. Unfortunately, in August 2018, the patient's ascites worsened, and adenocarcinoma cells were found by ascites biopsy. The patient passed away due to disease progression in September 2018.
